setup: Set the bench to about 30–45 degrees
Lie chest-down, chin just off the pad
execution: Raise your arms up and out in a Y
Lift to about ear height, then pause

notes: Use very light dumbbells; the long arms make a small weight feel heavy.
Keep the chest on the pad; lifting off it turns the movement into a back arch.
Lift only as high as you can without shrugging.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain in the shoulder that builds during the set
Numbness or tingling in the arm

regressions.name: No-weight Y-raise
regressions.reason: Learn the shoulder-blade position with the arms' weight only.

progressions.name: Pause at the top
progressions.reason: A 2-second hold adds work without more weight.

substitutions.name: Prone T-raise
substitutions.reason: Arms out straight to the sides; more mid-back.

substitutions.name: Face pull
substitutions.reason: Rear shoulder and upper back on a cable.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell rear-delt fly
substitutions.reason: Rear-shoulder raise with the arms out to the sides.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at bench height, figure lying chest-down on an incline bench, head to the right. Shows the arms rising from hanging straight down to in line with the body in a Y.

keyPositions.label: Hang
keyPositions.describe: Chest on the incline pad, feet on the floor. Arms hanging straight down from the shoulders, thumbs forward, light dumbbells.

keyPositions.label: Y
keyPositions.describe: Arms raised forward and out to about ear height, in line with the torso and angled out in a Y. Thumbs up, shoulder blades down. Chest still on the pad.

emphasise: Arms rise in a Y, thumbs up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
